does: Breaks cooked fish along its natural layers into large, tender pieces, taking out the skin and the bones as it goes.
how: Let the cooked fish cool enough to handle.
Peel away the skin and lift out any bones you can see or feel.
Press gently with a fork or your fingers so that the flesh parts along its layers, and stop while the flakes are still large.

cues.text: The flesh parts easily into layers under light pressure.
Large, moist flakes, not a paste.

mistakes.mistake: Mashing the fish to shreds, so that it disappears into a sauce or a mixture.
mistakes.fix: Break it once into big pieces and leave them; they break further when mixed.
Run your fingertips over every piece before it goes into the dish.

comes_after.why: Fish is flaked once it is cooked, and poaching is the gentlest way to cook it for flaking.
